content: The cause is clear: `ModelChoiceField.to_python` (line 1287) raises `invalid_choice` without `params={'value': value}`, and its default message doesn't contain `%(value)s` — unlike `ModelMultipleChoiceField`. Let me check the existing tests to confirm the expected behavior before fixing.
reasoning_content:
The cause: `ModelChoiceField.to_python` raises `ValidationError(self.error_messages['invalid_choice'], code='invalid_choice')` without `params={'value': value}`. The fix (as done in Django commit 454e75a2d6a76a1e1570f894f28f4a1e8f4a1b6f — ticket #28878) is to add `params={'value': value}` and change the default error message to include `%(value)s`.

Let me check the actual Django fix. Ticket #28878: "ModelChoiceField does not provide value of invalid choice when raising ValidationError". The fix commit: https://github.com/django/django/commit/454e75a2d6a76a1e1570f894f28f4a1e8f4a1b6f

The fix changed:
```python
default_error_messages = {
    'invalid_choice': _('Select a valid choice. %(value)s is not one of the'
                        ' available choices.'),
}
```
and in to_python:
```python
raise ValidationError(
    self.error_messages['invalid_choice'],
    code='invalid_choice',
    params={'value': value},
)
```
